newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent up on follow-through, relaxed on OPEC.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent up on follow-through, relaxed on OPEC.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were firmer on Tuesday in what traders said was a follow-through to late strength in the market on Monday.
August Brent was close to the market's opening levels at 1145 GMT and stood six cents a barrel firmer at $18.04. July gas oil was $1.25 a tonne up at $161.50.
"It is a continuation of strength from last night's close," one broker said. "We are looking to test higher numbers now."
Dealers said markets had largely ignored news from Vienna where OPEC ministers are gathering to meet on Wednesday.
Traders saw a rollover of the current 25.03 million barrels per day output ceiling and this expectation was reinforced by comments on Tuesday by Saudi Arabia's oil minister.
"A rollover is good if everyone adheres to their quota," Ali bin Ibrahim al-Naimi said.

Renewed tensions between the U.N. and Iraq provide a bullish backdrop for the meeting, and as a result prices have rallied this week through important technical resistance levels at around $18.00 a barrel.
Charles Gray at Prudential-Bache International Ltd. said prices could be given a sharp boost.
"The large swing to shorts could well fuel a price spike if we break through last week's highs at $18.32 and $19.47," he said.
